# TemperLoop

> TemperLoop makes Claude Code work the way a good engineering team works:
> agents pull tracked issues, build in isolated branches, and land every
> change as a reviewed, CI-gated pull request — safe to run in parallel,
> even unattended. A board adapter turns plain GitHub Issues into a
> cross-session work queue, Claude Code slash commands drive an issue from
> triage to a merged PR, and install/quality-gate tooling gets both running
> in a repo you already have.

TemperLoop is a toolkit — scripts, slash commands, and contract files you
read — not a hosted service or an app you depend on. It is Apache-2.0
licensed; see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what TemperLoop is, prerequisites, the testbed
  quickstart, the command map, repo layout, and the docs index.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): cross-agent operating instructions for a coding
  agent working in this repo — the CLI vs. `make` split, board-adapter
  rules and the shared API budget, quality gates, and the branch/PR/
  worktree safety rails.
- [Pitch](docs/pitch.md): the whole story on one page.
- [Who it's for](docs/who-its-for.md): the intended adopter, and who it
  deliberately isn't for.
- [Principles](docs/principles.md): the thesis and the fifteen design
  principles behind the kernel.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): how the board adapter, the
  build/sweep pipeline, and the guard hooks fit together.
- [Using the pipeline](docs/using-the-pipeline.md): the day-to-day
  operating guide.
- [Cost & autonomy](docs/cost-and-autonomy.md): what running it costs and
  what it does on its own.
- [Token spend](docs/token-spend.md): how it keeps model spend down and
  how to see where tokens went.
- [Feature docs](docs/features/): per-feature reference pages.
- [Managed merge queue](docs/managed-merge-queue.md): running the merge
  ladder end-to-end on a repo with no native GitHub merge queue.
- [Config precedence](docs/config-precedence.md): the six-layer config
  resolution ladder every tunable setting follows.
- [About](docs/about.md): where TemperLoop came from and who's behind it.
- [Contributing](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to contribute a feature doc, a
  failure-mode chapter, or a new adapter.
